The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2}{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$ Find $AC.$
worked_solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=6\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC, \\ m∠A & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 6\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘} \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 6\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}\,b}{2} \\ \frac{21\cancel{\sqrt{2}}}{\cancel{2}} & =\frac{3\cancel{\sqrt{2}}\,b}{\cancel{2}} \\ 3b & =21 \\ b & =7\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=7\,\text{cm}.$
